Thanks again for the call this morning  great to meet the FinCo team. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the performance and SLO items we talked through and propose next steps so we can get you a formal recommendation and cost estimate. Attaching a quick SLO matrix (redwood-slo-matrix.csv).

Summary of your targets (as I heard them):
- Latency: <= 250 ms median, <= 750 ms tail (99th) for single-turn prompts (for the bulk of traffic)
- Throughput: ~120 requests/sec steady state, with short bursts up to 250 req/s
- Concurrency: expected 25-40 concurrent active user streams
- Streaming: yes  you need token-by-token streaming for the assistant UI and partial output for latency-sensitive flows
- Context window: inputs up to ~8k tokens (document + query), outputs up to ~1k tokens for longer summarization flows

Key open items I noted we need to confirm:
1) Are the 8k token inputs a hard requirement for your 90% workload, or only for a small subset of users?
2) Do you have a preferred p95/p99 latency target for streaming (time-to-first-token) vs time-to-last-token?
3) Any constraints on cost vs latency tradeoff we should prioritize (e.g., strict latency at higher cost vs cost-savings at modestly higher latency)?

What to expect next:
- We (Redwood) will run a preliminary sizing + latency estimate: breakdown for typical request sizes (1k, 4k, 8k input tokens) and for streaming vs non-streaming.
- We'll propose a Dedicated config (GPU class, concurrency targets, batching settings) and a fallback Hosted profile for pilot.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min sync next week to review the SLO matrix and estimated latency numbers.

Next step from you: please confirm whether the 8k input window is required for ~90% of your queries or only for a long-tail set.

Thanks  talk soon.

Alex  thanks for the quick clarifications. I've attached a short PDF (context-window-latency-estimates.pdf) that summarizes how input size and output length map to expected latency on our serving profiles and the dominant performance factors. High-level notes below, and Vivek/Ethan are cc'ed to confirm the numbers.

High-level latency guidance (approx, single-request tail numbers on Redwood Dedicated medium profile when not batched):
- 1k input / 256 output: median ~90-120ms, p95 ~200-260ms
- 4k input / 512 output: median ~200-260ms, p95 ~430-520ms
- 8k input / 1k output: median ~420-520ms, p95 ~850-1,100ms

Why context window increases latency:
- KV cache growth: larger inputs require larger KV cache accesses per attention step, increasing per-token compute and memory bandwidth use.
- Attention compute scales roughly quadratically with sequence length in the attention phase; while optimized kernels reduce wall time, longer contexts still add per-step cost.
- First-token latency (time-to-first-token) is mostly driven by model startup and prefix processing  streaming mitigates perceived latency but the prefix still needs to be ingested/encoded.

Streaming impact and recommendations:
- If time-to-first-token target is <=150ms we recommend: enable prefix partial encoding + early-decode streaming, reduce batch windows to <5-10ms, and reserve small dedicated concurrency for streaming-critical requests to avoid queuing delays.
- For 8k-context streaming flows, we recommend pre-encoding commonly-shared document prefixes (cacheable) and issuing the query tokens separately to reduce initial delay.

Concurrency & throughput notes:
- With your target of 120 req/s and bursts to 250 req/s, Dedicated medium with horizontal autoscaling to 2-3 nodes should be sufficient (depending on model family/quantization).
- Concurrency of 30-50 streaming sessions requires careful routing to avoid head-of-line blocking; we suggest isolating streaming-critical traffic on a higher-priority queue.

Tradeoffs / cost levers:
- Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) reduces throughput cost but may increase CPU-side decoding time slightly; usually net positive for cost.
- Batching increases throughput efficiency but adds batching latency; we recommend aggressive batching for non-streaming bulk jobs and minimal batching for streaming.

Vivek/Ethan  can you confirm the estimate ranges above are aligned with our 80/20 medium profile numbers? If fine, we'll formalize into the SLO matrix and give FinCo a cost estimate.

--
Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa  quick confirmation from infra side:
- The p95 numbers Marissa shared align with our internal medium-profile microbenchmarks for the model family discussed (quantized). We expect variance +/- ~10-15% depending on tokenization and document structure.
- To hit <=150ms time-to-first-token for streaming we recommend: reserve a small streaming pool (4-6 concurrent reserved slots on medium nodes), enable prefix pre-encoding for commonly-shared doc fragments, and keep batch windows to <10ms. That will add predictable cost but keeps UX snappy.
- For FinCo's 120 req/s steady + 250 bursts: recommend starting with Dedicated medium x2 with autoscale to x3 for burst periods (policy-based). This balances cost and headroom; we'll include cost ranges in the SLO matrix.
